name.description: How the name the feature type, same as the property name.

fillColor.description: Color to use to fill the icon.

strokeColor.description: Color to use for the stroke around the icon.

drawingMode.description: How to render the icon, if any.

iconUri.description: URL of the image icon. Is not only used for point features, but also for polygons to recognize them in the legend and when showing the feature's properties. May optionally contain a matching pair of braces, which is replaced with the corresponding property value.

nameLabel.description: Property to use as the Name or title.

maxTitleResolution.description: At what zoom level should we stop showing the title. When zooming further out beyond this level, the title is no longer shown.

propertyTypeKeys.description: An ordered, semi-colon separated list of all property data keys to display when selecting the feature.

legendExpr.description: In the legend, show a summary of this feature.

stringFormat.description: A string that represents the .NET formatting to use for displaying the property value, e.g. {0:0,000.##} to show a thousand separator as well as up to two decimals.

expression.description: A formula that is computed upon loading the layer, and when the map's extent (bounding box) is changed. E.g. "sum(features, 'NR_PEOPLE')" sums the number of people within the extent of the map.

propertyTypeData.description: A list of property types, which specify how each feature's property should be displayed.

stringFormat.description: A string that represents the .NET formatting to use for displaying the property value, e.g. {0:0,000.##} to show a thousand separator as well as up to two decimals.

expression.title: Expression or formula
expression.description: A formula that is computed upon loading the layer. E.g. "properties.p_00_14_jr * properties.nr_people / 100" converts the percentage of children to an absolute number.

section.description: Separate the properties by placing each of them in their own section.

visibleInCallOut.description: If true (default), show the property when the feature is selected.

label.description: Property label, which is typically the same as this item's key. It is still useful, however, when you wish to display a property twice, each time using a different display format, e.g. text and link, or year and date separately.

description:
The map configuration defines two vector layers – **Roads** and **Parks** – each with its own visual style and metadata. Roads are rendered as a white‑filled polyline (fill #.ffffff, stroke #123456) with a stroke width of 2 px; the associated icon is “https://example.com/icons/road.png” (icon width 0 px, icon height 0 px, meaning the icon is used only in the legend). The road name is taken from the property **road_name**, and titles are shown down to zoom level 12. The road layer’s property list is ordered as “road_name;length;surface_type”. In the legend the total road length appears as a number formatted “{0:0,0.##} km” using the expression **sum(features, 'length')**, while the distinct surface types are displayed as plain text via **distinct(values(features, 'surface_type'))**.  

Parks are drawn as polygons with a fill colour #aadd55 and a stroke colour #654321, a stroke width of 1 px, and a 24 × 24 px icon whose URL “https://example.com/icons/park_{park_id}.png” inserts the park’s identifier. The park name comes from **park_name**, and titles stop rendering beyond zoom level 10. Its property order is “park_name;area;established”. The legend shows the total area of all parks as a number formatted “{0:0,0.0} ha” via **sum(features, 'area')**.  

The property‑type catalog specifies how each attribute should be displayed in call‑outs. **road_name** (“Road Name”) is a text field shown as “Name”. **length** (“Length (km)”) is a numeric field formatted “{0:0.##}”, calculated with the expression **properties.length / 1000**, grouped under the “Metrics” section and labelled “Length”. **surface_type** (“Surface Type”) is an options field under the “Details” section, labelled “Surface”. For parks, **park_name** (“Park Name”) appears as text labelled “Name”, **area** (“Area (ha)”) is a numeric field formatted “{0:0,0}” labelled “Area”, and **established** (“Established”) is a date field formatted “{0:yyyy}”, labelled “Year Established”. All of these properties are visible in call‑outs.
